analysis:
The PR changes only CHANGELOG.md, in the 'Unreleased - Autopilot daily earnings floor' section (head hunk at lines 2-9). It adds no source, config or schema changes, so no trust boundary, authorization path, encryption flow or billing code is modified in the supplied material.

The edits are prose describing planned economics behavior:
- Floor accrual ends after Nov 7, 2026 UTC, with Nov 7 settling at midnight Nov 8.
- Cohort baselines for machines with short history, taken from comparable mature machines with the same chip, performance tier and memory.
- Daily qualification requires trusted macOS 27+, at least 2 distinct downloaded eligible models, saved Autopilot consent, and at least 90% uptime with overlapping sessions and identity aliases merged.
- The baseline stays frozen through Autopilot off/on.

These statements touch A-009 (payment ledger) and A-015/A-016 (App Attest authorization) only as documented reward-eligibility rules. They echo the existing base-reward rule that requires macOS 27+ and current qualified App Attest.

The actual code is not in this diff, so I could not check the claims. Later passes that see the implementing code should check:
- Uptime and alias merging against T-055. Aliases and machine continuity are not unique hardware, so merged-alias uptime could be gamed.
- Cohort baseline derivation, since sponsored inference is counted and the comparable-cohort baseline could be manipulated.
- That the time-bound cutoff is enforced in code rather than only documented.
- That the 'OS claim' belongs to the same App Attest authorization as the qualification.

The changelog says the new financial tables are not yet covered by existing accounting archives. That is an existing documented residual, not a new finding.

No findings from this PR.
